sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Melbourne, FL?
sections.html:
Melbourne is a large city in southern Brevard County, so sellers deal with Brevard offices for taxes and records and with the city for permits and local rules. Your choices are a listing, a private sale or a cash offer, and a cash buyer mainly saves time and showings.

The city describes itself as the economic engine of Brevard County, with high-tech industry, a Space Coast location and ties to regional education and research leaders. Its own count, from the Bureau of Economic and Business Research for 2025, is 88,499 residents.

  • Confirm the parcel is inside city limits and which taxing districts bill it.
  • Gather permits for any work done on the house.
  • Get a payoff figure for every loan and lien.

Melbourne sits astride the Indian River Lagoon, with a large share of the city on the mainland and a portion on a barrier island. The lagoon separates the two, so the location of a house, mainland or beachside, can matter to buyers more than the city name.

The city covers 51.59 square miles, or 33,016.28 acres, as of March 2026. That is a large footprint for a city of its size, and it means a Melbourne address can mean very different neighborhoods, lots and ages of construction.

Melbourne has a council-manager charter. The council sets the annual budget and tax rate, and public hearings are held before new laws are approved and before the budget and property tax rate are finalized. Sellers who want to know whether the city's rate may change can watch those hearings.

sections.h2: Who handles Melbourne property taxes, and when are they due?
sections.html:
Brevard County's property appraiser values the property each January 1, and the county tax collector sends the bills. The city is one of several taxing authorities on a Melbourne bill.

Table 1 summarizes the statewide calendar the Department of Revenue prints for taxpayers.

Table 1. Florida property tax calendar, Department of Revenue
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date, at just value
March 1Deadline to apply for exemptions or classifications
AugustNotice of Proposed Property Taxes mailed
Within 25 days of the noticePetition to challenge value filed with the clerk
NovemberTax bills sent; 4 percent discount for November payment
April 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent
By June 1Tax certificates sold on unpaid items

The discount steps down to 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. Ask the Brevard tax collector for the current bill and for any amount owed on your parcel.

sections.h2: How do homestead and Save Our Homes affect a Melbourne seller?
sections.html:
Florida's homestead exemption is up to $50,000: the first $25,000 applies to all property taxes including school taxes, and an additional amount of up to $25,000 applies to assessed value over $50,000 and only to non-school taxes. The owner applies with the county property appraiser by March 1.

Save Our Homes limits yearly assessment increases to the lower of 3 percent or the change in the Consumer Price Index. The Department of Revenue's chart shows a 2.7 percent cap for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024, when the CPI change was 3.4 percent.

When a homestead sells, the buyer's assessment returns to just value the next January 1. A seller who buys another Florida home can port the benefit by filing the portability form with the homestead application by March 1, and the new homestead must be established within three years of January 1 of the year the old one was abandoned.

sections.h2: What does the deed cost in Brevard County?
sections.html:
Brevard falls under the standard state rate, which the Department of Revenue prints as 70 cents per $100 of consideration, with the exception of Miami-Dade. The clerk collects it when the deed is recorded, and all parties to the document are liable whichever side agrees to pay.

Consideration includes any mortgage or encumbrance on the property, whether or not the buyer assumes it. Clerk recording charges are $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus a $1.00 and $0.50 trust fund charge and a $4 per page technology charge.

  • Taxable deeds include warranty, special warranty, quit claim, trustee's and life estate deeds.
  • A deed in lieu of foreclosure and a certificate of title are also taxable.
  • A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed as not taxable.

sections.h2: What if the Melbourne house has a tenant, a lien or an unpaid tax bill?
sections.html:
Each of these needs to be cleared or priced before closing. For a tenant, Florida requires 3 days' written notice for unpaid rent, excluding weekends and court holidays, and a month-to-month tenancy ends with at least 30 days' notice.

Unpaid property tax can lead to a tax certificate. The tax collector awards each certificate to the bidder demanding the lowest interest rate, in quarter-percent steps. A holder may apply for a tax deed after two years from April 1 of the year of issuance, and homestead property with a small balance goes to the county rather than being sold at auction.

If the owner is behind on a mortgage, the clerk conducts the foreclosure sale not less than 20 days and not more than 35 days after final judgment, unless the plaintiff agrees to a longer period.

sections.h2: What about an inherited house in Melbourne?
sections.html:
Someone must have legal authority before a deed is signed. Florida's summary administration is available when the non-exempt estate does not exceed $150,000 or the decedent died more than two years ago.

Creditor claims are barred unless filed by the later of three months after first publication of the notice to creditors or 30 days after service on a required creditor. Florida has no estate tax for people who died after December 31, 2004, according to the Department of Revenue. Brevard's clerk and a probate attorney can say which path your estate needs.

sections.h2: How do I compare a Melbourne cash offer with listing?
sections.html:
Estimate what you would net from a listing after commission, repairs and carrying costs, then compare it with the written cash figure. The contract should say who pays the deed tax, title insurance and recording, when the closing is, and what happens to your deposit.

Do not pay a fee to get an offer, and do not sign a deed before the contract is final.

faqs.q: Which county is Melbourne, FL in?
faqs.a: Brevard County. The city's own page places Melbourne in southern Brevard County, southeast of Orlando on Florida's east coast, astride the Indian River Lagoon.

faqs.q: How many people live in Melbourne?
faqs.a: The city page gives 88,499 residents, citing the Bureau of Economic and Business Research for 2025.

faqs.q: What deed stamp tax rate applies in Brevard County?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue prints 70 cents per $100 for every county except Miami-Dade. The clerk collects it at recording and all parties to the deed are liable.

faqs.q: When must I apply for homestead exemption?
faqs.a: By March 1 of the tax year, with Form DR-501 to the county property appraiser, and the owner must have made the home a permanent residence by January 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Melbourne house that is in foreclosure?
faqs.a: Yes, if the sale closes and pays the lender before the court's sale takes place. The clerk's sale is set 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless the plaintiff agrees to longer, so ask the lender for the case status.
